openers.prompt_en: Read these lines from a funny poem: “Riya searched her schoolbag twice, / Her lunchbox sat beside her.” Where should you make a small pause: after “twice” or after “searched”?
openers.prompt_hi: Funny poem ki ye lines padho: “Riya searched her schoolbag twice, / Her lunchbox sat beside her.” Chhota pause kahaan loge: “twice” ke baad ya “searched” ke baad?
acceptable: at the end of the first line
hints: Where does the first line finish?
A line ending is a natural place for a small pause.
Read to the end of line one; pause after ___.
Pause after “twice” because it ends the first line.

openers.prompt_en: For a poem about a missing cricket bat, choose the line ending that rhymes with “play”: “We found the bat today” or “We found the bat at noon”?
openers.prompt_hi: Missing cricket bat wali poem mein “play” se rhyme karne wali line ending chuno: “We found the bat today” ya “We found the bat at noon”?
hints: Say “play” aloud. What sound ends it?
Compare the sounds, not just the letters.
The matching line ends with ___.
Choose “We found the bat today”; “today” rhymes with “play”.

harder.prompt_en: For a poem about a school play, choose the word that rhymes with “scene” despite different spelling: “green” or “sign”?
harder.prompt_hi: School play ki poem mein “scene” se rhyme karne wala word chuno, spelling alag hone par bhi: “green” ya “sign”?
harder.answer: green
hints: Say each option aloud after “scene”.
A rhyme depends on the ending sound.
“Scene” sounds like the ending of ___.
Choose “green”; it shares the ending sound of “scene”.

harder.prompt_en: Arjun searched the kitchen for his phone. His sister could see it in his shirt pocket, but Arjun kept looking. Why might this make readers laugh? Answer in a short phrase.
harder.prompt_hi: Arjun kitchen mein phone dhoondh raha tha. Uski behen ko phone uski shirt pocket mein dikh raha tha, par Arjun dhoondhta raha. Readers ko hansi kyun aa sakti hai? Chhote phrase mein batao.
harder.answer: Readers know the phone is in his pocket, but Arjun does not.
acceptable: He is searching for something in his own pocket.
We can see what Arjun cannot.
hints: Who knows where the phone is?
Compare what the reader knows with what Arjun knows.
Readers know ___, but Arjun does not.
Readers know it is in his pocket, but Arjun does not.

verified.solverAnswer: he kept looking while it was in his pocket

harder.prompt_en: A school notice reports one item of clothing left after sports day. Which is correct: “A trousers is in the lost-and-found box” or “A pair of trousers is in the lost-and-found box”?
harder.prompt_hi: Sports day ke baad ek clothing item lost-and-found box mein hai. Sahi notice chuno: “A trousers is in the lost-and-found box” ya “A pair of trousers is in the lost-and-found box”?
harder.answer: A pair of trousers is in the lost-and-found box
acceptable: a pair of trousers is in the lost-and-found box
hints: How do we name one clothing item called trousers?
This noun needs a phrase to show one item.
Write: A ___ of trousers is in the box.
Choose “A pair of trousers is”; “a pair of” means one item.

verified.solverAnswer: A pair of trousers is in the lost-and-found box

openers.prompt_en: At a school match, Meera packed her bat, reached the ground, and played her first ball. Complete: “First, Meera packed her bat. ___, she reached the ground.” Choose “Then” or “Finally”.
openers.prompt_hi: School match mein Meera ne bat pack kiya, ground pahunchi aur pehli ball kheli. Sentence poora karo: “First, Meera packed her bat. ___, she reached the ground.” “Then” ya “Finally”?
hints: Did reaching the ground happen at the end?
Choose the time word for an event between the first and last.
First she packed; ___ she reached the ground; finally she played.
Then fits because reaching the ground happened before she played.

openers.prompt_en: Yesterday, Aarav missed his metro stop and hurried back. Complete his story: “I ___ back to the previous station.” Choose “run” or “ran”.
openers.prompt_hi: Kal Aarav apna metro stop miss kar gaya aur jaldi wapas gaya. Uski story poori karo: “I ___ back to the previous station.” “run” ya “ran”?
hints: When did Aarav miss his stop?
A completed event needs the past form of the verb.
Yesterday I ___ back to the previous station.
Ran fits because Aarav is describing what happened yesterday.

harder.prompt_en: Change both verbs to the simple past: “Riya goes to the sports shop and buys a helmet.” Say the whole sentence.
harder.prompt_hi: Dono verbs ko simple past mein badlo: “Riya goes to the sports shop and buys a helmet.” Poora sentence bolo.
harder.answer: Riya went to the sports shop and bought a helmet.
acceptable: Riya went to the sports shop and bought a helmet
hints: How many actions must you change?
Both verbs have irregular past forms.
Riya ___ to the sports shop and ___ a helmet.
Riya went to the sports shop and bought a helmet; both actions are past.

verified.solverAnswer: Riya went to the sports shop and bought a helmet.

harder.prompt_en: The school bus pulled away. Nikhil checked his empty pocket, shouted “My pass!”, and ran after it. Why did Nikhil run after the bus?
harder.prompt_hi: School bus chal padi. Nikhil ne apni khaali pocket check ki, “My pass!” chillaya aur bus ke peeche dauda. Nikhil bus ke peeche kyun dauda?
harder.answer: He thought he had left his pass on the bus.
acceptable: He left his pass on the bus
He thought his bus pass was on the bus
hints: What did Nikhil notice just before running?
Connect his empty pocket with what he shouted.
He ran because he thought his ___ was on the bus.
He thought his pass was on the bus, so he ran after it.

harder.prompt_en: Complete this sentence with “slope”, “puddle”, “pile”, or “adventure”: “After the rain, the cyclists stopped because a deep ___ covered the narrow road.”
harder.prompt_hi: Is sentence ko “slope”, “puddle”, “pile”, ya “adventure” se poora karo: “After the rain, the cyclists stopped because a deep ___ covered the narrow road.”
harder.answer: puddle
hints: What might collect on a road after rain?
Look for a word that names standing water.
A deep ___ covered the narrow road.
Puddle fits because rainwater can collect on a road.

harder.prompt_en: A scooter rolled down a slope. Its rider jumped off, the scooter splashed through a puddle, and a guard stopped it. Which happened immediately before the guard stopped the scooter: the rider jumped off or it splashed through a puddle?
harder.prompt_hi: Scooter dhalaan se neeche ludhka. Savaar usse kood gaya, scooter paani ke gadde se guzra, aur guard ne use rok diya. Guard ke rokne se theek pehle kya hua: savaar kooda ya scooter paani ke gadde se guzra?
harder.answer: It splashed through a puddle
acceptable: the scooter splashed through a puddle
scooter paani ke gadde se guzra
hints: Which event comes just before the stopping?
Track the events in the order they are told.
The guard stopped it after the scooter ___.
It splashed through a puddle; that happened immediately before the guard stopped it.

harder.prompt_en: The scooter stopped beside a crowded market. Dev took a deep breath, checked that nobody was hurt, and only then smiled. How did Dev most likely feel when the scooter first stopped: relieved or excited?
harder.prompt_hi: Scooter bheed-bhaad wale bazaar ke paas ruka. Dev ne gehri saans li, dekha ki kisi ko chot toh nahi lagi, aur tab jaakar muskuraya. Scooter rukte hi Dev ko kaisa laga hoga: rahat mili ya utsaah hua?
harder.answer: Relieved
hints: What did Dev check before smiling?
His actions show he was concerned about safety.
After checking everyone, Dev felt ___.
Relieved; he smiled only after seeing that nobody was hurt.

harder.prompt_en: After the school trip, the teacher said, “Put the muddy shoes in a pile, not across the doorway.” Does “pile” mean a heap in one place or a row spread out?
harder.prompt_hi: School trip ke baad teacher ne kaha, “Keechad wale jooton ko ek pile mein rakho, darwaaze bhar mein mat phailaao.” Yahan “pile” ka matlab ek jagah dher hai ya phaili hui kataar?
harder.answer: A heap in one place
hints: What arrangement is the teacher asking for?
The contrast with ‘across the doorway’ helps.
The shoes should be gathered ___.
A heap in one place; the teacher does not want shoes spread out.

ongrade.prompt_en: At the metro station, Kabir found a lost phone, gave it to the help desk, and heard an announcement asking its owner to come forward. Which event should come after “then” in this retelling: finding the phone, giving it to the help desk, or hearing the announcement?
ongrade.prompt_hi: Metro station par Kabir ko khoya hua phone mila. Usne help desk par diya, phir owner ke liye announcement hui. Retelling mein ‘then’ ke baad kya aayega: phone milna, help desk par dena, ya announcement sunna?
ongrade.answer: giving it to the help desk
acceptable: giving the phone to the help desk
he gave it to the help desk
hints: Which event happened between finding the phone and the announcement?
‘Then’ introduces the event after the first one.
First he found it; then he ___.
He gave it to the help desk; that happened before the announcement.

ongrade.prompt_en: Complete this account of yesterday’s cricket match using the simple past: “The ball ___ (fly) over the boundary, and the crowd ___ (cheer).” Give both missing words in order.
ongrade.prompt_hi: Kal ke cricket match ka account simple past mein poora karo: ‘The ball ___ (fly) over the boundary, and the crowd ___ (cheer).’ Dono missing words order mein batao.
acceptable: the ball flew and the crowd cheered
hints: Did these actions happen yesterday or now?
One verb changes form; the other takes a past-tense ending.
fly → ___; cheer → ___.
Flew, cheered: both verbs describe completed actions yesterday.

ongrade.prompt_en: “The scooter rolled towards a busy road. Anaya called out to the riders, while her brother rushed to catch its handle.” Why did her brother rush: to stop the scooter reaching traffic, to ride it, or to look for Anaya?
ongrade.prompt_hi: ‘Scooter busy road ki taraf ludhak raha tha. Anaya ne riders ko awaaz di, aur uska bhai handle pakadne dauda.’ Bhai kyun dauda: scooter ko traffic tak pahunchne se rokne, use chalane, ya Anaya ko dhoondhne?
ongrade.answer: to stop the scooter reaching traffic
acceptable: to stop it reaching the road
to keep the scooter away from traffic
scooter ko traffic tak pahunchne se rokne
hints: Where was the scooter heading?
Use its direction and the brother’s action as clues.
He rushed to catch the handle before the scooter reached ___.
To stop it reaching traffic; he tried to catch the handle.

verified.solverAnswer: to stop the scooter reaching traffic

openers.prompt_en: A light display at the school concert follows rainbow colour order. After green and blue, which colour should appear before violet?
openers.prompt_hi: School concert ki light display rainbow colours ke order mein chalti hai. Green aur blue ke baad, violet se pehle kaunsa colour aayega?
hints: Can you recall the colours near the end of the rainbow?
Think of the colour placed between blue and violet.
Blue, ___, violet.
Indigo comes between blue and violet.

openers.prompt_en: A poem calls a rainbow above a football field ‘a painted gate in the sky’. Is the comparison about the rainbow’s curved shape or its sound?
openers.prompt_hi: Football field ke upar rainbow ko poem mein ‘sky mein painted gate’ kaha gaya hai. Yeh comparison uski curved shape se hai ya sound se?
hints: What do a gate and a rainbow look like?
Poems can compare how two things appear.
The comparison is about the rainbow’s ___.
Its curved shape makes it look like a gate.

harder.prompt_en: For a poem about a rainbow over a cricket ground, which line makes a comparison: ‘The rainbow appeared after rain’ or ‘The rainbow was a ribbon across the sky’?
harder.prompt_hi: Cricket ground ke upar rainbow wali poem ke liye kaunsi line comparison karti hai: ‘The rainbow appeared after rain’ ya ‘The rainbow was a ribbon across the sky’?
harder.answer: The rainbow was a ribbon across the sky
hints: Which line describes more than an event?
Look for a line that treats one thing as another.
The comparison is in the ___ line.
The ribbon line compares the rainbow’s long curve to a ribbon.

verified.solverAnswer: The rainbow was a ribbon across the sky

harder.prompt_en: After the monsoon shower, Meera saw sunlight sparkling on wet leaves. Complete her sentence with the best word: ‘The leaves looked ___ in the sunlight.’ Choose shining or dusty.
harder.prompt_hi: Monsoon shower ke baad Meera ne geele patton par dhoop chamakti dekhi. Sentence ke liye best word chuno: ‘The leaves looked ___ in the sunlight.’ Shining ya dusty?
harder.answer: Shining
hints: What does sunlight do on wet leaves?
Choose the word that matches sparkling.
The leaves looked ___ in the sunlight.
Shining fits because sunlight sparkles on the wet leaves.

harder.prompt_en: For a school exhibition label, choose the correctly spelt rainbow colour: indigo or indego?
harder.prompt_hi: School exhibition ke label ke liye rainbow colour ki correct spelling chuno: indigo ya indego?
harder.answer: indigo
hints: Which spelling have you seen in the rainbow colour list?
Pay attention to the vowel in the middle.
Write the colour as ind___o.
Indigo is correct; its middle vowel is i.

openers.prompt_en: At a school play, Meera lost her script. She asked Kabir for help. Kabir showed her the lines on his phone, and Meera finished the scene. Which happened first: Kabir showed the phone or Meera asked for help?
openers.prompt_hi: School play mein Meera ki script kho gayi. Usne Kabir se help maangi. Kabir ne phone par lines dikhayi, aur Meera ne scene poora kiya. Pehle kya hua: Kabir ne phone dikhaya ya Meera ne help maangi?
hints: What did Meera do after losing her script?
Follow the events in the order they are written.
Before Kabir showed his phone, Meera ____.
Meera asked for help; that happened before Kabir showed his phone.

openers.prompt_en: A cricket team kept bowling wide balls in practice. Their captain quietly placed a bottle near the crease. Soon the bowlers stopped stepping too far sideways. What was the captain's plan: remind them of the crease or end practice?
openers.prompt_hi: Cricket practice mein bowlers baar-baar wide ball daal rahe the. Captain ne chupchaap crease ke paas bottle rakhi. Phir bowlers sideways zyada aage jaana band kar gaye. Captain ka plan kya tha: crease yaad dilana ya practice khatam karna?
acceptable: To remind them of the crease
hints: What changed after the bottle was placed?
The bottle made an important boundary easier to notice.
The captain used the bottle to help bowlers notice the ____.
Remind them of the crease; the bottle made its position noticeable.

harder.prompt_en: A library book was always returned to the wrong shelf. The librarian put a bright label on its spine but said nothing. Next week, it was returned correctly. Why did the librarian use a label instead of giving a warning?
harder.prompt_hi: Library ki ek book hamesha galat shelf par lautayi jaati thi. Librarian ne uski spine par bright label lagaya, par kuch kaha nahi. Agle hafte book sahi jagah aayi. Warning dene ke bajay label kyun lagaya?
harder.answer: To help readers identify the correct shelf
acceptable: So readers could find the right shelf
The label reminded readers where the book belonged
hints: What problem did the librarian want to solve?
Think about what readers can learn from a visible label.
The label helped readers identify the correct ____.
It helped readers identify the correct shelf without a spoken warning.

verified.solverAnswer: A label guides silently without causing embarrassment.

harder.prompt_en: Choose the correctly written sentence: A. Riya told, "The match starts at four." B. Riya said, "The match starts at four." C. Riya said Aarav, "The match starts at four."
harder.prompt_hi: Sahi likha sentence chuno: A. Riya told, "The match starts at four." B. Riya said, "The match starts at four." C. Riya said Aarav, "The match starts at four."
harder.answer: B
acceptable: Riya said, "The match starts at four."
hints: Which reporting verb works without naming a listener?
Check whether the verb needs someone after it.
Without a named listener, choose option ____.
B; ‘said’ works here without naming a listener.

harder.prompt_en: Complete the school notice with a word from the same family as ‘free’: ‘Students may choose any book for the reading hour. This ______ helps them discover new interests.’
harder.prompt_hi: School notice ko ‘free’ ki word family wale shabd se poora karo: ‘Students may choose any book for the reading hour. This ______ helps them discover new interests.’
harder.answer: freedom
hints: What does choosing any book give the students?
Use the noun form of ‘free’ to name that choice.
The noun form of ‘free’ is ____.
Freedom; it names the ability to choose.

openers.prompt_en: Read these line endings from a poem about a pond: rain / light / train / night. Do the endings rhyme in an ABAB or AABB pattern?
openers.prompt_hi: Pond wali poem ki lines ke end words padho: rain / light / train / night. Inka rhyme pattern ABAB hai ya AABB?
hints: Which two endings sound alike?
Give matching sounds the same letter.
Write the letters in line order: __.
ABAB: rain matches train, and light matches night.

openers.prompt_en: In a school science diary, Meera writes: 'The eggs hatched. Later, the young swimmers grew legs.' What stage came between the eggs and the swimmers with legs?
openers.prompt_hi: School science diary mein Meera likhti hai: 'Eggs hatch hue. Baad mein young swimmers ke legs aa gaye.' Eggs aur legs wale stage ke beech kaunsa stage tha?
hints: What comes out of a frog’s egg?
Think of the swimming stage before legs appear.
The missing stage is a __.
Tadpole: it swims before it grows legs.

harder.prompt_en: A pond diary shows eggs, then tadpoles, then frogs. A classmate says this is the complete order. Which stage is missing, and where does it go?
harder.prompt_hi: Pond diary mein eggs, phir tadpoles, phir frogs likha hai. Classmate kehta hai order complete hai. Kaunsa stage missing hai, aur woh kahan aayega?
harder.answer: Tadpole with legs, between tadpole and frog
acceptable: a tadpole with legs after the tadpole
hints: Does a swimmer become a frog without changing first?
Look for the stage when legs have appeared.
Put __ between tadpole and frog.
Tadpole with legs goes between tadpole and frog.

verified.solverAnswer: tadpoles with legs, between tadpoles and frogs

harder.prompt_en: Complete both sentences with the correct forms of 'leap': 'One frog ___ onto the bank. Three frogs ___ after it.' Say the two words in order.
harder.prompt_hi: 'Leap' ke sahi forms se dono sentences complete karo: 'One frog ___ onto the bank. Three frogs ___ after it.' Dono words order mein bolo.
harder.answer: leaps; leap
hints: Is each subject one frog or more than one?
In the present tense, a singular subject takes a different ending.
One frog __; three frogs __.
Leaps; leap: the singular subject takes -s, but the plural does not.

harder.prompt_en: At a wetland survey, Ayaan counts 14 young swimmers with tails but no legs. Complete his report with one word: 'I saw 14 ___ in the pond.'
harder.prompt_hi: Wetland survey mein Ayaan 14 young swimmers dekhta hai jinki tails hain, par legs nahi. Report ek word se complete karo: 'I saw 14 ___ in the pond.'
harder.answer: tadpoles
hints: Which frog-life stage has a tail but no legs?
The number tells you to use the plural form.
I saw 14 __ in the pond.
Tadpoles: they have tails, and 14 needs a plural noun.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'Our school collects rain from the roof in a large drum. The gardening club uses it on dry days.' What is the main idea: collecting rain for later use, the size of the drum, or the gardening club?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'Our school collects rain from the roof in a large drum. The gardening club uses it on dry days.' Main idea kya hai: collecting rain for later use, drum ka size, ya gardening club?
hints: Which choice covers both sentences?
Look for what the school does and why.
The passage is mainly about collecting rain for ____.
Collecting rain for later use covers both the drum and its purpose.

openers.prompt_en: Read: 'A village pond has a stone border. During heavy rain, the border keeps muddy water from the road out of the pond.' Why is the stone border useful: it keeps road mud out, or it makes rain fall?
openers.prompt_hi: Padho: 'A village pond has a stone border. During heavy rain, the border keeps muddy water from the road out of the pond.' Stone border useful kyun hai: road ka mud rokta hai, ya rain karwata hai?
acceptable: stops mud from entering the pond
hints: What reaches the pond from the road?
Notice what the border keeps outside.
The border stops ____ from entering.
It keeps road mud out, helping protect the pond water.

harder.prompt_en: Read: 'A covered tank receives rain through a pipe with a mesh screen. The screen catches leaves before the water enters.' Why might the stored water stay cleaner: the mesh catches leaves, or the cover creates rain?
harder.prompt_hi: Padho: 'A covered tank receives rain through a pipe with a mesh screen. The screen catches leaves before the water enters.' Stored water cleaner kyun rahega: mesh leaves pakadta hai, ya cover rain banata hai?
harder.answer: the mesh catches leaves
acceptable: leaves are stopped before entering the tank
hints: What travels through the pipe besides water?
Think about what happens before water enters the tank.
The water stays cleaner because ____ cannot enter.
The mesh catches leaves before they enter the tank.

harder.prompt_en: The school keeps rainwater in a tank for use next month. Complete the notice with one word: 'We ____ rainwater for the dry season.' Choose store, underground, or stepwell.
harder.prompt_hi: School next month ke liye tank mein rainwater rakhta hai. Notice mein ek word bharo: 'We ____ rainwater for the dry season.' Choose karo: store, underground, ya stepwell.
harder.answer: store
hints: What action does the school take with the water?
The blank needs an action word.
We ____ rainwater for the dry season.
Store fits: the school keeps water for later use.

harder.prompt_en: After a school event, you notice a tap running beside the water station. Complete a polite suggestion using 'should' and an action word: 'We should ____.'
harder.prompt_hi: School event ke baad water station ke paas tap chalta hua dikhta hai. 'Should' aur action word se polite suggestion poora karo: 'We should ____.'
harder.answer: turn off the tap
hints: What action would stop the water flowing?
Put the action word directly after 'should'.
We should ____ the tap.
We should turn off the tap to avoid wasting water.

verified.solverAnswer: We should turn off the tap.

openers.prompt_en: Read this line from a poem about kho-kho: “Dash! Neha races past the line.” Which word should you say with extra force to bring out the sudden movement: “Dash” or “line”?
openers.prompt_hi: Kho-kho ki poem ki yeh line padho: “Dash! Neha races past the line.” Achanak movement dikhane ke liye kis word par zyada zor doge: “Dash” ya “line”?
hints: Which word makes the movement sound sudden?
An exclamation mark can guide how you say a word.
I would stress “___” to make the action lively.
Dash: stressing the exclamation brings out the sudden run.

openers.prompt_en: At a school fair, children use chalk to make a hopscotch grid and play for hours. Which message fits better: “Fun needs expensive equipment” or “Simple games can bring joy”?
openers.prompt_hi: School fair mein bachche chalk se hopscotch ka grid banakar ghanton khelte hain. Kaunsa message sahi hai: “Fun needs expensive equipment” ya “Simple games can bring joy”?
hints: What did the children use to start playing?
Compare the cost of their equipment with their enjoyment.
The fair shows that ___ can bring joy.
Simple games can bring joy: chalk was enough for hours of play.

harder.prompt_en: A poem says, “Our empty pockets did not stop the match; we marked a court in dust.” Why do the players mention their empty pockets?
harder.prompt_hi: Ek poem kehti hai, “Our empty pockets did not stop the match; we marked a court in dust.” Players apni empty pockets ka zikr kyun karte hain?
harder.answer: To show they could enjoy playing without spending money
acceptable: Games can be fun without costly equipment
They did not need money to play
hints: Did having no money stop their match?
Notice what they used instead of bought equipment.
The contrast shows they could play without ___.
They enjoyed playing without spending money: a dust court was enough.

verified.solverAnswer: They had no money for expensive games.

harder.prompt_en: For a schoolyard game, first draw a circle. Next toss a marker inside it. Then jump to the marker. Which instruction belongs between “Draw a circle” and “Jump to the marker”: “Toss the marker” or “Erase the circle”?
harder.prompt_hi: Schoolyard game mein pehle circle banao, phir marker usmein phenko, aur uske baad marker tak jump karo. “Draw a circle” aur “Jump to the marker” ke beech kaunsi instruction aayegi: “Toss the marker” ya “Erase the circle”?
harder.answer: Toss the marker
acceptable: throw the marker inside the circle
hints: What must happen before you jump towards the marker?
Follow the order given by first, next, and then.
Draw a circle → ___ → jump to the marker.
Toss the marker: it must be inside before you jump towards it.

harder.prompt_en: A class compares two games. Choose the correct sentence: “Kho-kho is more exciting than ludo but more faster” or “Kho-kho is more exciting than ludo but faster.”
harder.prompt_hi: Class do games compare kar rahi hai. Sahi sentence chuno: “Kho-kho is more exciting than ludo but more faster” ya “Kho-kho is more exciting than ludo but faster.”
harder.answer: Kho-kho is more exciting than ludo but faster.
acceptable: Kho-kho is more exciting than ludo but faster
hints: Look closely at the two words used to compare speed.
A comparative ending and “more” do not go together.
Keep “more exciting,” but change “more faster” to ___.
Kho-kho is more exciting than ludo but faster: never use “more faster.”

verified.solverAnswer: Kho-kho is more exciting than ludo but faster.

openers.prompt_en: At a school fair, Riya paid for a game but her name was missing from the list. She showed her receipt, and the organiser added her name. What solved Riya’s problem?
openers.prompt_hi: School fair mein Riya ne game ke paise diye, par list mein uska naam nahi tha. Usne receipt dikhayi, aur organiser ne naam jod diya. Riya ki problem kaise solve hui?
openers.answer: She showed her receipt, so the organiser added her name.
acceptable: Riya showed her receipt and got her name added
The organiser added her name after seeing the receipt
hints: What proof did Riya have?
Find the action that made the organiser change the list.
Riya showed her ___; then the organiser acted.
Her receipt proved she had paid, so her name was added.

openers.prompt_en: Aarav checked every team’s cricket score by the same rule, including his own team’s. Was he fair or selfish? Give one reason.
openers.prompt_hi: Aarav ne har cricket team ka score ek hi rule se check kiya, apni team ka bhi. Woh fair tha ya selfish? Ek reason do.
openers.answer: Fair, because he used the same rule for every team.
acceptable: Fair, since he did not favour his own team
hints: Did Aarav make an exception for his team?
Notice whether the rule changed from team to team.
He was ___ because the rule stayed the same.
He was fair: he applied the same rule to every team.

verified.solverAnswer: Fair, because he applied the same rule to everyone.

harder.prompt_en: During a kabaddi match, Neha reported her own team’s extra point, though it meant losing. Which describes Neha better—honest or selfish? Give the detail that proves it.
harder.prompt_hi: Kabaddi match mein Neha ne apni team ka extra point report kiya, bhale hi team haar gayi. Neha ke liye honest ya selfish—kaunsa word better hai? Proof bhi batao.
harder.answer: Honest, because she reported her own team’s extra point.
acceptable: Honest—she admitted her team had an extra point
Honest, since she told the truth even though her team lost
hints: Which choice might have helped Neha’s team win?
Compare what benefited her team with what she actually said.
She was ___ because she reported ___.
Neha was honest: she reported the extra point despite the loss.

verified.solverAnswer: Honest, because she reported her own team’s extra point.

harder.prompt_en: Two friends want the last seat on a school trip. The teacher gives it to the student who signed up first. Why is this decision fair?
